title: Split Array Into Maximum Number of Subarrays
statement:
`nums` holds non-negative integers. The score of a contiguous, non-empty piece of `nums` is the bitwise AND of all of its elements.

Cut `nums` into one or more contiguous pieces so that every element lies in exactly one piece. Among the cuttings whose scores add up to the smallest possible total, return the largest number of pieces any of them has.
notes:
## Intuition

AND never sets a bit, so any piece's score is at least the AND of the whole array, and adding more pieces can only add more non-negative scores. So the smallest possible total is exactly `AND(nums)`, reached by keeping everything in one piece.

- If `AND(nums)` is not 0, two or more pieces would each score at least that much and the total would grow, so the answer is `1`.
- If it is 0, every piece must score 0. Then cut greedily: close a piece the moment its running AND hits 0. Closing as early as possible leaves the most room for later pieces, and any leftover tail (whose AND is not 0) can be glued onto the last closed piece, since AND with 0 stays 0.

A DP over every cut position also works but costs O(n²).

## Approach

1. Set `count` to 0 and `current` to `-1` (all bits set, the identity for AND).
2. For each `value`, update `current &= value`.
3. When `current` becomes 0, one more zero-score piece is done: add one to `count` and reset `current` to `-1`.
4. Return `max(count, 1)`: if no piece ever reached 0, the whole array is the single piece.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 0, 2, 0, 1, 2]`. `current` becomes `1`, then `1 & 0 = 0`, so `count = 1`. Next `2`, then `2 & 0 = 0`, so `count = 2`. Next `1`, then `1 & 2 = 0`, so `count = 3`. The answer is `3`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass over `nums`.
- Space: O(1): two counters.

## Pitfalls

- Return at least `1`: an array like `[5, 7, 1, 3]` never reaches 0, and `count` stays 0.
- Starting `current` at 0 instead of all bits set makes every AND 0 immediately.
- A leftover tail with a non-zero AND is not a separate piece; it joins the previous one.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `count` | number of zero-score pieces closed so far |
| `current` | AND of the piece being built (`-1` when it is empty) |
| `value` | the element being added to the current piece |

narration.2: No piece has been closed yet.
narration.3: -1 has every bit set, so ANDing it with the first value gives that value.
narration.4: Add the elements one by one to the piece being built.
narration.5: AND only clears bits, so the piece's score can only drop.
narration.6: The piece already scores 0; closing it now leaves the most elements for later pieces.
narration.11: If no piece reached 0, the whole array is one piece; any leftover tail joins the last piece.
